input.content:
# Per-tool access gate

## Context

`mcp-server` today has exactly two authorization gates, both all-or-nothing:

- **Whole-server gate** — `hasAccess()` in [mcp-server.js:96-102](nodes/mcp-server.js#L96-L102), closure-scoped, untested.
- **Admin-tools gate** — `isAdmin()` in [oauth-discovery.js:10-16](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L10-L16), pure and tested, but only covers `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

There is nothing in between. Every `mcp-in` tool on a server is visible and callable by every
caller who clears the whole-server gate, so the only way to give one group access to a subset of
tools is to split them across separate `mcp-server` nodes — duplicating path, OIDC config,
credentials and discovery routes.

This adds a third, finer gate: **per tool**, configured on the `mcp-in` node. Unauthorized tools
disappear from `tools/list` and from the `initialize` instructions, and a direct `tools/call`
is refused with an explanatory `isError` result — the same behaviour the admin gate already has.

Decisions taken with the user:

- **Value semantics:** comma-separated list, any-of. `media, admin` → the claim must contain at
  least one. A single value behaves exactly as today.
- **Claim name:** taken from the server's `Required claim` (Auth tab) only. No per-tool override —
  each `mcp-in` supplies only a *value*.
- **Visibility:** unauthorized tools are hidden from `tools/list` and `initialize`; a direct call
  is still denied with a reason.

## Implementation

### 1. New `lib/claim-gate.js` — one shared, list-aware gate

The three gates run byte-identical logic today. Extract it once, teach it the any-of list, and
have all three call it. A new file rather than growing `lib/oauth-discovery.js`, whose header
comment scopes it to OAuth discovery — `isAdmin` was always a misfit there.

```js
// claimAllows(claims, claimName, requiredValue)
//   requiredValue '' / undefined        → allow (any authenticated caller)
//   claims null/undefined               → deny
//   requiredValue 'a, b'                → allow if claim contains 'a' OR 'b'
//   claim value array                   → membership test
//   claim value scalar                  → equality against any listed value
```

Split on **comma only**, then `trim()` each item and drop empties — splitting on whitespace too
would break a group name containing a space, which the current exact-match gates accept.

Also export a pure `visibleTools(registeredTools, claims, requiredClaim)` that returns the
`tools/list` array (schema normalisation from [mcp-server.js:249-253](nodes/mcp-server.js#L249-L253)
plus the per-tool filter). That moves the one piece of new decision logic out of the closure and
into something the existing Mocha suite can actually reach — nothing under `nodes/` is testable
today.

`lib/oauth-discovery.js` keeps exporting `isAdmin` as a thin wrapper over `claimAllows` so
[mcp-server.js:9](nodes/mcp-server.js#L9) and `test/oauth-discovery.test.js` are untouched.

> **Note — deliberate widening:** routing all three gates through `claimAllows` means an existing
> whole-server or admin `Required value` that literally contains a comma stops matching as one
> literal string and becomes an any-of list. Realistically nobody has such a value, and the new
> behaviour is the more useful one; it will be documented in the README. Say the word if you'd
> rather keep the two old gates on strict single-value matching.

### 2. `nodes/mcp-in.js` + `nodes/mcp-in.html` — the per-tool value

- New config prop `requiredValue` (default `''`), added to `defaults` in
  [mcp-in.html:71-80](nodes/mcp-in.html#L71-L80).
- Editor UI: one `form-row` + `form-tips` after **Timeout**, separated by an `<hr>`, following the
  `exposeClaims` block's style ([mcp-in.html:30-37](nodes/mcp-in.html#L30-L37)). Placeholder
  `(empty = anyone who can reach this server)`; tip explains that the claim *name* comes from the
  MCP Server node's Auth tab and that unauthorized callers never see the tool.
- Pass it through at [mcp-in.js:26](nodes/mcp-in.js#L26) as a 5th positional argument to
  `registerMCPTool` — the only call site.
- Extend the `data-help-name="mcp-in"` block with a short paragraph on the gate.

### 3. `nodes/mcp-server.js` — store it and enforce it

- `registerMCPTool(name, description, schema, timeoutSec, requiredValue)`
  ([mcp-server.js:144](nodes/mcp-server.js#L144)) stores `requiredValue` on the registry entry.
  A stale `mcp-in` calling with four arguments yields `undefined` → open, matching today's default.
- Replace the closure `hasAccess` body with a `claimAllows` call (keep the name and the comment).
- Add, next to `adminAllowed` at [mcp-server.js:223](nodes/mcp-server.js#L223):
  `const toolAllowed = name => claimAllows(claims, requiredClaim, (node.mcpRegisteredTools[name] || {}).requiredValue);`
- Three enforcement points, mirroring how `adminAllowed` is already threaded through:
  - `initialize` ([:229-232](nodes/mcp-server.js#L229-L232)) — filter the dynamic tool names with `toolAllowed`.
  - `tools/list` ([:248-255](nodes/mcp-server.js#L248-L255)) — replace the loop with `visibleTools(...)`.
  - `tools/call` ([:266](nodes/mcp-server.js#L266)) — inside the `if (node.mcpRegisteredTools[toolName])`
    branch, before generating the callId: if `!toolAllowed(toolName)`, set
    `node.status({ fill:'red', shape:'ring', text:'forbidden' })` and return `denied(...)`, worded
    like the admin denial at [:294-295](nodes/mcp-server.js#L294-L295) — name the tool, say it is a

# Per-tool access gate

## Context

`mcp-server` today has two authorization gates, both all-or-nothing:

- **Whole-server gate** — `hasAccess()` in [mcp-server.js:96-102](nodes/mcp-server.js#L96-L102), closure-scoped, untested.
- **Admin-tools gate** — `isAdmin()` in [oauth-discovery.js:10-16](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L10-L16), pure and tested, but only covers `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

There is nothing in between. Every `mcp-in` tool on a server is visible and callable by everyone
who clears the whole-server gate, so giving one group access to a subset of tools means splitting
them across separate `mcp-server` nodes — duplicating path, OIDC config, credentials and
discovery routes.

This adds a per-tool gate on `mcp-in`, and in doing so collapses the whole thing into **one
coherent model**: one claim name on the server, everything else is values.

## The model

**One claim name.** The server's `Required claim` (Auth tab, default `groups`) is the only claim
name in the system. `adminRequiredClaim` is removed — the admin gate matches against the server's
claim too.

**Everything else is a value**, and every value is a comma-separated any-of list (`media, ops` →
the claim must contain at least one). A single value behaves exactly as today.

| Value | Set on | Grants |
|---|---|---|
| Server `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth tab | Blanket access to every tool on this server. Empty (default) = every authenticated caller has it. |
| Tool `Required value` | mcp-in (new) | That one tool. Empty = the tool is covered by the blanket grant only. |

# Per-tool access gate

## Context

`mcp-server` today has exactly two authorization gates, both all-or-nothing:

- **Whole-server gate** — `hasAccess()` in [mcp-server.js:96-102](nodes/mcp-server.js#L96-L102), closure-scoped, untested.
- **Admin-tools gate** — `isAdmin()` in [oauth-discovery.js:10-16](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L10-L16), pure and tested, but only covers `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

There is nothing in between. Every `mcp-in` tool on a server is visible and callable by every
caller who clears the whole-server gate, so the only way to give one group access to a subset of
tools is to split them across separate `mcp-server` nodes — duplicating path, OIDC config,
credentials and discovery routes.

This adds a third, finer gate: **per tool**, configured on the `mcp-in` node. Unauthorized tools
disappear from `tools/list` and from the `initialize` instructions, and a direct `tools/call`
is refused with an explanatory `isError` result — the same behaviour the admin gate already has.

Decisions taken with the user:

- **Value semantics:** comma-separated list, any-of. `media, admin` → the claim must contain at
  least one. A single value behaves exactly as today.
- **Claim name:** taken from the server's `Required claim` (Auth tab) only. No per-tool override —
  each `mcp-in` supplies only a *value*.
- **Visibility:** unauthorized tools are hidden from `tools/list` and `initialize`; a direct call
  is still denied with a reason.

## Implementation

### 1. New `lib/claim-gate.js` — one shared, list-aware gate

The three gates run byte-identical logic today. Extract it once, teach it the any-of list, and
have all three call it. A new file rather than growing `lib/oauth-discovery.js`, whose header
comment scopes it to OAuth discovery — `isAdmin` was always a misfit there.

```js
// claimAllows(claims, claimName, requiredValue)
//   requiredValue '' / undefined        → allow (any authenticated caller)
//   claims null/undefined               → deny
//   requiredValue 'a, b'                → allow if claim contains 'a' OR 'b'
//   claim value array                   → membership test
//   claim value scalar                  → equality against any listed value
```

Split on **comma only**, then `trim()` each item and drop empties — splitting on whitespace too
would break a group name containing a space, which the current exact-match gates accept.

Also export a pure `visibleTools(registeredTools, claims, requiredClaim)` that returns the
`tools/list` array (schema normalisation from [mcp-server.js:249-253](nodes/mcp-server.js#L249-L253)
plus the per-tool filter). That moves the one piece of new decision logic out of the closure and
into something the existing Mocha suite can actually reach — nothing under `nodes/` is testable
today.

`lib/oauth-discovery.js` keeps exporting `isAdmin` as a thin wrapper over `claimAllows` so
[mcp-server.js:9](nodes/mcp-server.js#L9) and `test/oauth-discovery.test.js` are untouched.

> **Note — deliberate widening:** routing all three gates through `claimAllows` means an existing
> whole-server or admin `Required value` that literally contains a comma stops matching as one
> literal string and becomes an any-of list. Realistically nobody has such a value, and the new

- **Admin-tools gate** — `isAdmin()` in [oauth-discovery.js:10-16](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L10-L16), pure and tested, but only covers `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

There is nothing in between. Every `mcp-in` tool on a server is visible and callable by everyone
who clears the whole-server gate, so giving one group access to a subset of tools means splitting
them across separate `mcp-server` nodes — duplicating path, OIDC config, credentials and
discovery routes.

This adds a per-tool gate on `mcp-in`, and in doing so collapses the whole thing into **one
coherent model**: one claim name on the server, everything else is values.

## The model

**One claim name.** The server's `Required claim` (Auth tab, default `groups`) is the only claim
name in the system. `adminRequiredClaim` is removed — the admin gate matches against the server's
claim too.

**Everything else is a value**, and every value is a comma-separated any-of list (`media, ops` →
the claim must contain at least one). A single value behaves exactly as today.

| Value | Set on | Grants |
|---|---|---|
| Server `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth tab | Blanket access to every tool on this server. Empty (default) = every authenticated caller has it. |
| Tool `Required value` | mcp-in (new) | That one tool. Empty = the tool is covered by the blanket grant only. |
| Admin `Required value` | mcp-server, Admin tab | `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`. Empty = they fall back to the blanket grant. |

**Grants are a union, not a chain.** Holding a tool's value is enough on its own — you do not also
need the server's value. Everyone with a valid token connects (as today); what differs is what
they see.

```
requiredClaim: groups     server value: staff
tool A: (no value)   tool B: media   tool C: ops   admin value: admin

groups=[staff]  → A, B, C          (blanket)
groups=[media]  → B                (tool value alone suffices)
groups=[admin]  → get_flow/deploy_flow
groups=[guest]  → nothing
server value empty → everyone gets the blanket grant: A, B, C
```

**One deliberate exception: admin tools.** The blanket grant does *not* reach them when an admin
value is set — `staff` above sees A/B/C but not `get_flow`. Admin tools are privileged
infrastructure and always require their own key; anything else would silently widen access for
existing deployments. Only when the admin value is left empty do they fall back to the blanket
grant, which is exactly today's behaviour.

Expressed as one predicate, where `grants(value)` is false for an empty value:

```
serverGranted    = !serverValue || grants(serverValue)
toolAllowed(t)   = grants(t.requiredValue) || serverGranted
adminAllowed     = adminToolsEnabled && (adminValue ? grants(adminValue) : serverGranted)
```

The two existing gates run byte-identical logic. Extract it once, teach it the any-of list, and

  value grants nothing; "empty means allow" is a policy decision, not a matching rule). Null

  membership and scalar claims by equality against any listed item.

  preserving today's semantics.
- `createToolGate({ claims, claimName, serverValue })` → `{ serverGranted, allows(toolValue) }`,
  implementing the two predicates above. This is where the new decision logic lives, deliberately
  outside the node closure so the existing Mocha suite can reach it — nothing under `nodes/` is
  testable today.
- `visibleTools(registeredTools, gate)` — the `tools/list` array: the schema normalisation from
  [mcp-server.js:249-253](nodes/mcp-server.js#L249-L253) plus the filter.

`lib/oauth-discovery.js` keeps exporting `isAdmin` as a thin wrapper over `claimAllows`, so

# Per-tool access gate

## Context

`mcp-server` today has two authorization gates, both all-or-nothing:

- **Whole-server gate** — `hasAccess()` in [mcp-server.js:96-102](nodes/mcp-server.js#L96-L102), closure-scoped, untested.
- **Admin-tools gate** — `isAdmin()` in [oauth-discovery.js:10-16](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L10-L16), pure and tested, but only covers `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

There is nothing in between. Every `mcp-in` tool on a server is visible and callable by everyone
who clears the whole-server gate, so giving one group access to a subset of tools means splitting
them across separate `mcp-server` nodes — duplicating path, OIDC config, credentials and
discovery routes.

This adds a per-tool gate on `mcp-in`, and in doing so collapses all three gates into **one rule
with no exceptions**.

## The model

**One claim name.** The server's `Required claim` (Auth tab, default `groups`) is the only claim
name in the system. `adminRequiredClaim` is removed — the admin gate matches against the server's
claim too.

**Everything else is a value**, and every value is a comma-separated any-of list (`media, ops` →
the claim must contain at least one). A single value behaves exactly as today.

| Value | Set on | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Server `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth tab | The **default** for every tool that doesn't set its own. Empty (default) = every authenticated caller passes. |
| Tool `Required value` | mcp-in (new) | Governs that tool **alone**, overriding the server default. |
| Admin `Required value` | mcp-server, Admin tab | Same thing for `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`. |

**The nearest value wins, and it is the only one that applies.** A tool with its own value is
governed by that value and nothing else — the server's value neither widens nor narrows it. This
is why there is no admin carve-out: the admin gate is just a gated tool like any other.

```
allowedFor(value) = value ? grants(value) : serverGranted
serverGranted     = !serverValue || grants(serverValue)
```

`grants(v)` = the caller's claim contains at least one item of the comma-separated list `v`.

```
requiredClaim: groups     server value: staff
tool A: (no value)   tool B: media   admin value: admin

groups=[staff]        → A
groups=[media]        → B
groups=[staff,media]  → A, B
groups=[admin]        → get_flow, deploy_flow
groups=[guest]        → nothing
server value empty    → everyone gets A
```

Holding a tool's value is enough on its own — you do not also need the server's value. Everyone
with a valid token still connects, exactly as today; only what they see differs.

## Implementation

### 1. New `lib/claim-gate.js`

The two existing gates run byte-identical logic. Extract it once, teach it the any-of list, and
have everything call it. A new file rather than growing `lib/oauth-discovery.js`, whose header
comment scopes it to OAuth discovery — `isAdmin` was always a misfit there.

Exports:

- `grants(claims, claimName, value)` — the primitive. Empty/undefined `value` → `false` (an empty
  value grants nothing; "empty means fall back" is a policy decision, not a matching rule). Null
  claims → `false`. Splits `value` on **comma only**, trims, drops empties; matches array claims by
  membership and scalar claims by equality against any listed item.
- `claimAllows(claims, claimName, value)` = `!value || grants(...)` — the allow-on-empty variant,
  preserving today's semantics for `isAdmin`.
- `createToolGate({ claims, claimName, serverValue })` → `{ serverGranted, allows(value) }`,
  implementing the two lines above. This is where the new decision logic lives, deliberately
  outside the node closure so the existing Mocha suite can reach it — nothing under `nodes/` is
  testable today.
- `visibleTools(registeredTools, gate)` — the `tools/list` array: the schema normalisation from
  [mcp-server.js:249-253](nodes/mcp-server.js#L249-L253) plus the filter.

`lib/oauth-discovery.js` keeps exporting `isAdmin` as a thin wrapper over `claimAllows`, so
`test/oauth-discovery.test.js` stays green untouched.

> **Note — deliberate widening:** routing the old gates through the shared code means an existing
> server or admin `Required value` that literally contains a comma stops matching as one literal
> string and becomes an any-of list. Realistically nobody has such a value, and the new behaviour
> is the more useful one; it goes in the README.

### 2. `nodes/mcp-in.js` + `nodes/mcp-in.html` — the per-tool value

- New config prop `requiredValue` (default `''`) in
  [mcp-in.html:71-80](nodes/mcp-in.html#L71-L80).
- Editor UI: one `form-row` + `form-tips` after **Timeout**, behind an `<hr>`, styled like the
  `exposeClaims` block ([mcp-in.html:30-37](nodes/mcp-in.html#L30-L37)). Placeholder
  `(empty = use the server's default)`; the tip states that the claim *name* comes from the MCP
  Server node's Auth tab, that the list is comma-separated any-of, and that a value here replaces
  the server's default for this tool rather than adding to it.
- Pass it through at [mcp-in.js:26](nodes/mcp-in.js#L26) as a 5th positional argument to
  `registerMCPTool` — the only call site.
- Add a short paragraph to the `data-help-name="mcp-in"` block.

### 3. `nodes/mcp-server.js` — store it, drop the admin claim, enforce per tool

- `registerMCPTool(name, description, schema, timeoutSec, requiredValue)`
  ([:144](nodes/mcp-server.js#L144)) stores `requiredValue` on the registry entry. A stale `mcp-in`
  calling with four arguments yields `undefined` → server default, matching today's behaviour.
- Delete `adminRequiredClaim` ([:131](nodes/mcp-server.js#L131)); the admin gate uses
  `requiredClaim`.
- Replace the closure `hasAccess` ([:96-102](nodes/mcp-server.js#L96-L102)) with a per-request
  `const gate = createToolGate({ claims, claimName: requiredClaim, serverValue: requiredValue })`
  built right after `requireBearer` ([:205-208](nodes/mcp-server.js#L205-L208)).
- `adminAllowed` ([:223](nodes/mcp-server.js#L223)) becomes
  `adminToolsEnabled && gate.allows(adminRequiredValue)` — the `allowed &&` prefix goes away, so an
  admin-value-only caller gets in.
- Three enforcement points, mirroring how `adminAllowed` is already threaded through:
  - `initialize` ([:229-232](nodes/mcp-server.js#L229-L232)) — filter the dynamic tool names with
    `gate.allows(...)`; the `allowed ? ... : []` wrapper disappears, the per-tool filter subsumes it.
  - `tools/list` ([:246-256](nodes/mcp-server.js#L246-L256)) — drop the
    `if (!allowed) return respond({ tools: [] })` early return and replace the loop with
    `visibleTools(node.mcpRegisteredTools, gate)`.
  - `tools/call` ([:258-266](nodes/mcp-server.js#L258-L266)) — drop the blanket `if (!allowed)`
    denial; inside the `if (node.mcpRegisteredTools[toolName])` branch, before generating the
    callId, deny when `!gate.allows(entry.requiredValue)`: red `forbidden` status plus `denied(...)`
    worded like the admin denial at [:294-295](nodes/mcp-server.js#L294-L295) — name the tool, say
    it is a permission restriction and not a tool error.
- The admin branch's own re-check ([:292-296](nodes/mcp-server.js#L292-L296)) stays, rewritten to
  `gate.allows(adminRequiredValue)`, so admin tools keep being verified per call and not just at
  listing time.
- Unknown-tool responses keep returning `-32601` unchanged; a direct call on a known-but-forbidden
  tool still gets the explanatory `isError` text, as the admin tools do today.

### 4. `nodes/mcp-server.html`

- Remove the `adminRequiredClaim` form-row ([:126-129](nodes/mcp-server.html#L126-L129)) and its
  `defaults` entry ([:180](nodes/mcp-server.html#L180)); reword the Admin tip
  ([:134-136](nodes/mcp-server.html#L134-L136)) to reference the Auth tab's claim.
- Reword the Auth-tab tip ([:105-107](nodes/mcp-server.html#L105-L107)): this claim name is used by
  every gate, and this value is the default for tools that don't set their own — no longer a wall
  in front of them.

### 5. Docs and examples

- README **Access control** (`README.md:54-69`) — replace "Two independent, optional gates" with the
  table, the rule and the worked example above, plus the list syntax.
- Strip the now-ignored `"adminRequiredClaim": "groups"` key from the embedded `mcp-server` node in
  all nine `examples/*.json` (e.g. `examples/docker-mcp.json:28`). Every one already sets it to
  `groups`, identical to `requiredClaim`, so this is cosmetic — no example changes behaviour.
- **Migration note for the README:** two behaviour changes for existing configs, both narrow.
  A flow that set `adminRequiredClaim` to something *other* than `requiredClaim` has its admin gate
  move to the server's claim name. And a server value that previously also had to be satisfied
  before the admin gate is now bypassed for callers holding only the admin value.

## Verification

1. `npm test` — the four existing suites stay green; new `test/claim-gate.test.js` covers
   `grants` (empty value → false, null claims, scalar match, array match, any-of list, whitespace
   around items, `a,,b`, missing claim), `claimAllows` (allow-on-empty), `createToolGate` (the full
   truth table from the worked example, including empty server value) and `visibleTools` (filters,
   normalises a bare-properties schema, passes an object schema through).
2. Manual end-to-end against a running Node-RED with a **Local debug token** set — that path
   short-circuits to claims `{ sub:'debug', name:'Local debug user', groups:['admin'] }`
   ([mcp-auth.js:119-121](lib/mcp-auth.js#L119-L121)), so no IdP is needed. Three `mcp-in` tools on
   one server: `requiredValue` empty, `admin`, and `nope`. All calls carry
   `Authorization: Bearer <debug token>` against `POST /mcp/<path>`.
   - Server value empty → `tools/list` shows the open tool and the `admin` one, not `nope`.
   - Server value `staff` → **only** the `admin` tool. This is the load-bearing case: the open tool
     drops out (no blanket grant) while the gated one stays (its own value suffices).
   - `tools/call` on `nope` → HTTP 200, `result.isError === true`, explanatory text.
   - `tools/call` on the `admin` tool → the flow fires and `mcp-out` resolves normally.
   - `initialize` → `instructions` names exactly the visible tools.
3. Admin tools: with admin value `superuser` the debug caller sees no `get_flow` regardless of the
   server value; with admin value `admin` it appears and `get_flow` returns a flow.

# Per-tool access gate

## Context

`mcp-server` today has two authorization gates, both all-or-nothing:

- **Whole-server gate** — `hasAccess()` in [mcp-server.js:96-102](nodes/mcp-server.js#L96-L102), closure-scoped, untested.
- **Admin-tools gate** — `isAdmin()` in [oauth-discovery.js:10-16](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L10-L16), pure and tested, but only covers `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

There is nothing in between. Every `mcp-in` tool on a server is visible and callable by everyone
who clears the whole-server gate, so giving one group access to a subset of tools means splitting
them across separate `mcp-server` nodes — duplicating path, OIDC config, credentials and
discovery routes.

This adds a per-tool gate on `mcp-in`, and in doing so collapses all three gates into **one rule
with no exceptions**.

## The model

**One claim name.** The server's `Required claim` (Auth tab, default `groups`) is the only claim
name in the system. `adminRequiredClaim` is removed — the admin gate matches against the server's
claim too.

**Everything else is a value**, and every value is a comma-separated any-of list (`media, ops` →
the claim must contain at least one). A single value behaves exactly as today.

| Value | Set on | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Server `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth tab | The **default** for every tool that doesn't set its own. Empty (default) = every authenticated caller passes. |
| Tool `Required value` | mcp-in (new) | Governs that tool **alone**, overriding the server default. |
| Admin `Required value` | mcp-server, Admin tab | Same thing for `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`. |

**The nearest value wins, and it is the only one that applies.** A tool with its own value is
governed by that value and nothing else — the server's value neither widens nor narrows it. This
is why there is no admin carve-out: the admin gate is just a gated tool like any other.

```
allowedFor(value) = value ? grants(value) : serverGranted
serverGranted     = !serverValue || grants(serverValue)
```

`grants(v)` = the caller's claim contains at least one item of the comma-separated list `v`.

```
requiredClaim: groups     server value: staff
tool A: (no value)   tool B: media   admin value: admin

groups=[staff]        → A
groups=[media]        → B
groups=[staff,media]  → A, B
groups=[admin]        → get_flow, deploy_flow
groups=[guest]        → nothing
server value empty    → everyone gets A
```

Holding a tool's value is enough on its own — you do not also need the server's value. Everyone
with a valid token still connects, exactly as today; only what they see differs.

## Implementation

### 1. New `lib/claim-gate.js`

The two existing gates run byte-identical logic. Extract it once, teach it the any-of list, and
have everything call it. A new file rather than growing `lib/oauth-discovery.js`, whose header
comment scopes it to OAuth discovery — `isAdmin` was always a misfit there.

Exports:

- `grants(claims, claimName, value)` — the primitive. Empty/undefined `value` → `false` (an empty
  value grants nothing; "empty means fall back" is a policy decision, not a matching rule). Null
  claims → `false`. Splits `value` on **comma only**, trims, drops empties; matches array claims by
  membership and scalar claims by equality against any listed item.
- `claimAllows(claims, claimName, value)` = `!value || grants(...)` — the allow-on-empty variant,
  preserving today's semantics for `isAdmin`.
- `createToolGate({ claims, claimName, serverValue })` → `{ serverGranted, allows(value) }`,
  implementing the two lines above. This is where the new decision logic lives, deliberately
  outside the node closure so the existing Mocha suite can reach it — nothing under `nodes/` is
  testable today.
- `visibleTools(registeredTools, gate)` — the `tools/list` array: the schema normalisation from
  [mcp-server.js:249-253](nodes/mcp-server.js#L249-L253) plus the filter.

`lib/oauth-discovery.js` keeps exporting `isAdmin` as a thin wrapper over `claimAllows`, so
`test/oauth-discovery.test.js` stays green untouched.

> **Note — deliberate widening:** routing the old gates through the shared code means an existing
> server or admin `Required value` that literally contains a comma stops matching as one literal
> string and becomes an any-of list. Realistically nobody has such a value, and the new behaviour
> is the more useful one; it goes in the README.

### 2. `nodes/mcp-in.js` + `nodes/mcp-in.html` — the per-tool value

- Editor UI: one `form-row` + `form-tips` after **Timeout**, behind an `<hr>`, styled like the

  the server's default for this tool rather than adding to it.
- Pass it through at [mcp-in.js:26](nodes/mcp-in.js#L26) as a 5th positional argument to

# Per-tool access gate

## Context

`mcp-server` today has two authorization gates, both all-or-nothing:

- **Whole-server gate** — `hasAccess()` in [mcp-server.js:96-102](nodes/mcp-server.js#L96-L102), closure-scoped, untested.
- **Admin-tools gate** — `isAdmin()` in [oauth-discovery.js:10-16](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L10-L16), pure and tested, but only covers `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

There is nothing in between. Every `mcp-in` tool on a server is visible and callable by everyone
who clears the whole-server gate, so giving one group access to a subset of tools means splitting
them across separate `mcp-server` nodes — duplicating path, OIDC config, credentials and
discovery routes.

This adds a per-tool gate on `mcp-in` and unifies all three gates under a single rule, with no
special cases anywhere.

## The model

**One claim name.** The server's `Required claim` (Auth tab, default `groups`) is the only claim
name in the system. `adminRequiredClaim` is removed — the admin gate matches against the server's
claim too.

**Every other field is a value list.** Comma-separated, any-of: `media, ops` passes if the claim
contains at least one of them. A single value behaves exactly as today. An empty list means "no
constraint from this field".

| Field | Set on | Constrains |
|---|---|---|
| Server `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth tab | Every tool on the server. |
| Tool `Required value` | mcp-in (new) | That one tool, additionally. |
| Admin `Required value` | mcp-server, Admin tab | `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`, additionally. |

**Gates are AND-ed.** Reaching a tool means clearing the server's list *and* that tool's list. An
empty list is satisfied by anyone. Admin tools are not special: their field is simply the tool
list for `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

```
passes(list)   = !list || claim contains at least one item of list
allowedFor(v)  = passes(serverValue) && passes(v)

adminAllowed   = adminToolsEnabled && allowedFor(adminValue)
toolAllowed(t) = allowedFor(t.requiredValue)
```

```
requiredClaim: groups     server value: staff
tool A: (empty)   tool B: media   admin value: admin

groups=[staff]         → A
groups=[staff, media]  → A, B
groups=[staff, admin]  → A + get_flow, deploy_flow
groups=[media]         → nothing            (server list not cleared)
groups=[guest]         → nothing

server value empty:
groups=[media]         → A, B
groups=[guest]         → A
```

Everyone with a valid token still connects, exactly as today; only what they see differs.

## Implementation

### 1. New `lib/claim-gate.js`

The two existing gates run byte-identical logic. Extract it once, teach it the comma-separated
list, and have everything call it. A new file rather than growing `lib/oauth-discovery.js`, whose
header comment scopes it to OAuth discovery — `isAdmin` was always a misfit there.

Exports:

- `grants(claims, claimName, list)` — the primitive. Empty/undefined `list` → `false` (an empty
  list matches nothing; "empty means no constraint" is a policy decision, not a matching rule).
  Null claims → `false`. Splits on **comma only**, trims, drops empties; matches array claims by
  membership and scalar claims by equality against any listed item.
- `claimAllows(claims, claimName, list)` = `!list || grants(...)` — the `passes()` above, i.e.
  today's semantics generalised to a list.
- `createToolGate({ claims, claimName, serverValue })` → `{ serverGranted, allows(list) }`, where
  `allows(list) = serverGranted && claimAllows(list)`. This is where the new decision logic lives,
  deliberately outside the node closure so the existing Mocha suite can reach it — nothing under
  `nodes/` is testable today.

  [mcp-server.js:249-253](nodes/mcp-server.js#L249-L253) plus the filter.

- **Admin**: enable/disable admin tools, admin token (for the Node-RED Admin API), admin API
  port, and the required-value gate that additionally restricts just the admin tools.

### Access control

**One claim name, many value lists.** `Required claim` on the Auth tab (default `groups`) names
the single JWT claim every gate matches against. Every other authorization field is a
comma-separated **any-of** list of values — `media, ops` passes if the claim contains at least one
of them. An empty list imposes no restriction.

| Field | Where | Restricts |
|---|---|---|
| `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth tab | every tool on this server |
| `Required value` | mcp-in | that one tool, additionally |
| `Required value` | mcp-server, Admin tab | `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`, additionally |

**The lists are combined with AND.** Reaching a tool means clearing the server's list *and* that
tool's own list. Admin tools are not a special case — their field is simply the tool list for
`get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

```
Required claim: groups     server value: staff
tool A: (empty)   tool B: media   admin value: admin

groups=[staff]         → A
groups=[staff, media]  → A, B
groups=[staff, admin]  → A + get_flow, deploy_flow
groups=[media]         → nothing            (server list not cleared)
groups=[guest]         → nothing

server value empty:
groups=[media]         → A, B
groups=[guest]         → A
```

Everyone with a valid token still connects — `initialize` always succeeds — but tools a caller
can't reach are hidden from `tools/list` and from the `initialize` instructions. A direct
`tools/call` on one of them is refused as an MCP tool result with `isError: true` and an
explanatory message (not a raw JSON-RPC protocol error), so the reason reaches the calling model
instead of being collapsed into a generic "tool execution failed".

> **Upgrading:** the admin gate no longer has its own claim-name field — it matches against the
> Auth tab's `Required claim` like everything else. If you had set a *different* claim name for
> admin tools, move that value to the Auth tab or adjust the admin list accordingly. A value that
> literally contains a comma is now read as a list rather than one literal string.

# @frtnbach/node-red-contrib-mcp-server

Generic [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server nodes for
Node-RED: expose any flow as an MCP tool behind an OAuth-protected endpoint, with optional
Node-RED admin (flow read/deploy) tools. No home-automation or other domain coupling — this
is a bare building block for turning Node-RED flows into MCP tools that AI assistants
(Claude, etc.) can call.

## Nodes

- **`mcp-server`** (config node) — hosts a standalone MCP JSON-RPC endpoint at
  `POST /mcp/<path>`, OAuth 2.0 protected-resource discovery (RFC 9728), authorization-server
  discovery (RFC 8414) proxying a real OIDC identity provider, and a dynamic client
  registration shim, so OAuth-aware MCP clients (e.g. Claude.ai) can self-register and
  authenticate. Multiple `mcp-server` nodes can coexist, each with its own path and its own
  independent auth configuration.
- **`mcp-in`** — defines one MCP tool (name, description, JSON-Schema parameters). When an
  MCP client calls the tool, the node emits a message carrying the call arguments; wire the
  rest of the flow to do the actual work.
- **`mcp-out`** — resolves a pending tool call. Wire the end of your flow here with
  `msg._mcpCallId` intact (from the originating `mcp-in` message) and `msg.payload` set to
  the result.

A single `mcp-in` → ... → `mcp-out` chain is one MCP tool. Build as many chains as you want
against the same `mcp-server` node to expose a whole toolset.

## Admin tools

Enable **Admin tools** on an `mcp-server` node to additionally expose two tools that operate
on Node-RED's own Admin HTTP API, gated by a configurable JWT claim (default: `groups`
contains `admin`):

- **`get_flow`** — lists all flow tabs (id, label, node count), or returns the full JSON of
  one tab when called with an `id`.
- **`deploy_flow`** — creates or updates a flow tab.

## Configuring an `mcp-server` node

- **General**: name, `path` (→ registers `POST /mcp/<path>`), the public `Server URL` this
  Node-RED instance is reachable at, optional server name/instructions shown to the model, and
  an optional **hostname filter** (see below).
- **Auth**: an OIDC `Identity provider` issuer URL (**required** — endpoints auto-discovered
  from `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, with PocketID-style fallback paths; leaving this
  empty produces a broken OAuth discovery document with relative-path endpoints and no working
  auth, so the editor won't let you deploy without it), client id/secret (leave the secret
  empty to run as a public/PKCE client — recommended), **required** redirect URIs (defaults to
  Claude.ai's callback), scopes, token audience, an optional local debug token that bypasses
  the IdP entirely for local testing (put any placeholder URL in Identity provider and rely on
  the debug token — it's never contacted when the debug token matches), and a whole-server
  **required claim/value gate** (see below, unrelated despite the similar name).
- **Admin**: enable/disable admin tools, admin token (for the Node-RED Admin API), admin API
  port, and the required claim/value gate that additionally restricts just the admin tools.

### Access control

Two independent, optional gates:

- **Whole-server gate** (Auth tab, `Required claim`/`Required value`): when a value is set, the
  validated token's claim must contain it for *any* of this server's tools — including admin
  tools — to be usable. Callers who fail the check still connect (`initialize` succeeds) but see
  no tools and any `tools/call` is refused with a human-readable reason. Leave the value empty
  (the default) to allow all authenticated users.
- **Admin-only gate** (Admin tab): the same shape, but only gates `get_flow`/`deploy_flow` —
  ordinary tools defined by `mcp-in`/`mcp-out` remain usable by anyone who passes the
  whole-server gate above.

Both denials are returned as an MCP tool result with `isError: true` and an explanatory message
(not a raw JSON-RPC protocol error), so the reason reaches the calling model instead of being
collapsed into a generic "tool execution failed".

### Hostname filtering

Off by default. When **Only serve requests for this hostname** is enabled, the node only answers
requests whose `Host` header matches the hostname in its `Server URL`. This lets several
`mcp-server` nodes share the *same* `path` on one Node-RED instance, each answering only its own
virtual host — useful behind a reverse proxy that fronts multiple hostnames for one Node-RED
backend. Leave it off for a single server, or when a reverse proxy rewrites the `Host` header.

### Reverse proxy

Each `mcp-server` node is its own OAuth resource — unlike a single shared MCP endpoint, every
instance registers **its own** discovery and registration routes, scoped under its `path`. For
a node with `path: docker` and `Server URL: https://mcp.example.com`, these six routes exist:

| Method & path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /mcp/docker` | The JSON-RPC MCP endpoint (bearer-token protected) |
| `GET /mcp/docker/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` | Resource metadata (RFC 9728), path-inserted form |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/docker` | Resource metadata (RFC 9728), RFC 8414 form |
| `GET /mcp/docker/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | Auth-server metadata (RFC 8414), path-inserted form |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/docker` | Auth-server metadata (RFC 8414), RFC 8414 form |
| `POST /mcp/docker/oauth/register` | Dynamic client registration shim |

Both well-known forms are advertised because different MCP clients probe different ones —
expose both. Since every instance's routes share the `/mcp/<path>` and `/.well-known/*/mcp/<path>`
shapes, **one set of wildcard rules covers every current and future `mcp-server` node** (as long
as they're all reachable through the same domain/upstream) — no reverse-proxy change needed when
adding a new `path`. Example, using
[Caddy](https://caddyserver.com/) via [caddy-docker-proxy](https://github.com/lucaslorentz/caddy-docker-proxy)
labels:

```yaml
labels:
  caddy_1: mcp.example.com
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_0: /mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_1: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_2: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
```

Node-RED itself 404s any path that isn't an actual registered route, so the wildcard doesn't
expose anything beyond what each deployed `mcp-server` node already registers. If a `path`
needs to be reachable on a *different* domain than the others, give it its own `caddy_N` site
block (or combine with [hostname filtering](#hostname-filtering) above).

**What the identity provider needs to support** (same requirements as `lib/mcp-auth.js`):

- An **OIDC provider with discovery** — endpoints are read from
  `‹issuerUrl›/.well-known/openid-configuration`, falling back to PocketID's path layout if
  discovery is unavailable.
- **JWT access tokens** signed with a key published on the provider's **JWKS** (tokens are
  verified locally; opaque/introspection-only access tokens are not supported).
- A client configured with the **redirect URI(s)** from the node's *Redirect URIs* setting,
  grant types `authorization_code` + `refresh_token`, **PKCE (S256)**, and — if a client secret
  is set — `client_secret_post` auth. Leave the secret empty to run as a public/PKCE client
  (recommended).

> Tested with **Caddy** (reverse proxy) + **PocketID** (identity provider) + **Claude.ai** (MCP
> client). Any spec-compliant OIDC provider issuing JWT access tokens, behind any reverse proxy
> that forwards the routes above, should work the same way.

## Examples

See [`examples/`](examples/) for nine ready-to-import flows (Jellyfin, Calibre, Docker,
Music Assistant, Radarr, iRobot/rest980, Overseerr, Sonarr, Spotify), each with its own
`mcp-server` node (server description pre-filled, `Server URL`/`Identity provider` left
blank for you to fill in) and `mcp-in`/`mcp-out` tools — a good reference for wiring up
your own tools.

## Development

```
npm install
npm test
```

## License

# @frtnbach/node-red-contrib-mcp-server

Generic [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server nodes for
Node-RED: expose any flow as an MCP tool behind an OAuth-protected endpoint, with optional
Node-RED admin (flow read/deploy) tools. No home-automation or other domain coupling — this
is a bare building block for turning Node-RED flows into MCP tools that AI assistants
(Claude, etc.) can call.

## Nodes

- **`mcp-server`** (config node) — hosts a standalone MCP JSON-RPC endpoint at
  `POST /mcp/<path>`, OAuth 2.0 protected-resource discovery (RFC 9728), authorization-server
  discovery (RFC 8414) proxying a real OIDC identity provider, and a dynamic client
  registration shim, so OAuth-aware MCP clients (e.g. Claude.ai) can self-register and
  authenticate. Multiple `mcp-server` nodes can coexist, each with its own path and its own
  independent auth configuration.
- **`mcp-in`** — defines one MCP tool (name, description, JSON-Schema parameters). When an
  MCP client calls the tool, the node emits a message carrying the call arguments; wire the
  rest of the flow to do the actual work.
- **`mcp-out`** — resolves a pending tool call. Wire the end of your flow here with
  `msg._mcpCallId` intact (from the originating `mcp-in` message) and `msg.payload` set to
  the result.

A single `mcp-in` → ... → `mcp-out` chain is one MCP tool. Build as many chains as you want
against the same `mcp-server` node to expose a whole toolset.

## Admin tools

Enable **Admin tools** on an `mcp-server` node to additionally expose two tools that operate
on Node-RED's own Admin HTTP API, gated by a configurable JWT claim (default: `groups`
contains `admin`):

- **`get_flow`** — lists all flow tabs (id, label, node count), or returns the full JSON of
  one tab when called with an `id`.
- **`deploy_flow`** — creates or updates a flow tab.

## Configuring an `mcp-server` node

- **General**: name, `path` (→ registers `POST /mcp/<path>`), the public `Server URL` this
  Node-RED instance is reachable at, optional server name/instructions shown to the model, and
  an optional **hostname filter** (see below).
- **Auth**: an OIDC `Identity provider` issuer URL (**required** — endpoints auto-discovered
  from `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, with PocketID-style fallback paths; leaving this
  empty produces a broken OAuth discovery document with relative-path endpoints and no working
  auth, so the editor won't let you deploy without it), client id/secret (leave the secret
  empty to run as a public/PKCE client — recommended), **required** redirect URIs (defaults to
  Claude.ai's callback), scopes, token audience, an optional local debug token that bypasses
  the IdP entirely for local testing (put any placeholder URL in Identity provider and rely on
  the debug token — it's never contacted when the debug token matches), and a whole-server
  **required claim/value gate** (see below, unrelated despite the similar name).
- **Admin**: enable/disable admin tools, admin token (for the Node-RED Admin API), admin API
  port, and the required-value gate that additionally restricts just the admin tools.

### Access control

**One claim name, many value lists.** `Required claim` on the Auth tab (default `groups`) names
the single JWT claim every gate matches against. Every other authorization field is a
comma-separated **any-of** list of values — `media, ops` passes if the claim contains at least one
of them. An empty list imposes no restriction.

| Field | Where | Restricts |
|---|---|---|
| `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth tab | every tool on this server |
| `Required value` | mcp-in | that one tool, additionally |
| `Required value` | mcp-server, Admin tab | `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`, additionally |

**The lists are combined with AND.** Reaching a tool means clearing the server's list *and* that
tool's own list. Admin tools are not a special case — their field is simply the tool list for
`get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

```
Required claim: groups     server value: staff
tool A: (empty)   tool B: media   admin value: admin

groups=[staff]         → A
groups=[staff, media]  → A, B
groups=[staff, admin]  → A + get_flow, deploy_flow
groups=[media]         → nothing            (server list not cleared)
groups=[guest]         → nothing

server value empty:
groups=[media]         → A, B
groups=[guest]         → A
```

Everyone with a valid token still connects — `initialize` always succeeds — but tools a caller
can't reach are hidden from `tools/list` and from the `initialize` instructions. A direct
`tools/call` on one of them is refused as an MCP tool result with `isError: true` and an
explanatory message (not a raw JSON-RPC protocol error), so the reason reaches the calling model
instead of being collapsed into a generic "tool execution failed".

> **Upgrading:** the admin gate no longer has its own claim-name field — it matches against the
> Auth tab's `Required claim` like everything else. If you had set a *different* claim name for
> admin tools, move that value to the Auth tab or adjust the admin list accordingly. A value that
> literally contains a comma is now read as a list rather than one literal string.

### Hostname filtering

Off by default. When **Only serve requests for this hostname** is enabled, the node only answers
requests whose `Host` header matches the hostname in its `Server URL`. This lets several
`mcp-server` nodes share the *same* `path` on one Node-RED instance, each answering only its own
virtual host — useful behind a reverse proxy that fronts multiple hostnames for one Node-RED
backend. Leave it off for a single server, or when a reverse proxy rewrites the `Host` header.

### Reverse proxy

Each `mcp-server` node is its own OAuth resource — unlike a single shared MCP endpoint, every
instance registers **its own** discovery and registration routes, scoped under its `path`. For
a node with `path: docker` and `Server URL: https://mcp.example.com`, these six routes exist:

| Method & path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /mcp/docker` | The JSON-RPC MCP endpoint (bearer-token protected) |
| `GET /mcp/docker/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` | Resource metadata (RFC 9728), path-inserted form |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/docker` | Resource metadata (RFC 9728), RFC 8414 form |
| `GET /mcp/docker/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | Auth-server metadata (RFC 8414), path-inserted form |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/docker` | Auth-server metadata (RFC 8414), RFC 8414 form |
| `POST /mcp/docker/oauth/register` | Dynamic client registration shim |

Both well-known forms are advertised because different MCP clients probe different ones —
expose both. Since every instance's routes share the `/mcp/<path>` and `/.well-known/*/mcp/<path>`
shapes, **one set of wildcard rules covers every current and future `mcp-server` node** (as long
as they're all reachable through the same domain/upstream) — no reverse-proxy change needed when
adding a new `path`. Example, using
[Caddy](https://caddyserver.com/) via [caddy-docker-proxy](https://github.com/lucaslorentz/caddy-docker-proxy)
labels:

```yaml
labels:
  caddy_1: mcp.example.com
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_0: /mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_1: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_2: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
```

Node-RED itself 404s any path that isn't an actual registered route, so the wildcard doesn't
expose anything beyond what each deployed `mcp-server` node already registers. If a `path`
needs to be reachable on a *different* domain than the others, give it its own `caddy_N` site
block (or combine with [hostname filtering](#hostname-filtering) above).

**What the identity provider needs to support** (same requirements as `lib/mcp-auth.js`):

- An **OIDC provider with discovery** — endpoints are read from
  `‹issuerUrl›/.well-known/openid-configuration`, falling back to PocketID's path layout if
  discovery is unavailable.
- **JWT access tokens** signed with a key published on the provider's **JWKS** (tokens are
  verified locally; opaque/introspection-only access tokens are not supported).
- A client configured with the **redirect URI(s)** from the node's *Redirect URIs* setting,
  grant types `authorization_code` + `refresh_token`, **PKCE (S256)**, and — if a client secret
  is set — `client_secret_post` auth. Leave the secret empty to run as a public/PKCE client
  (recommended).

> Tested with **Caddy** (reverse proxy) + **PocketID** (identity provider) + **Claude.ai** (MCP
> client). Any spec-compliant OIDC provider issuing JWT access tokens, behind any reverse proxy
> that forwards the routes above, should work the same way.

## Examples

See [`examples/`](examples/) for nine ready-to-import flows (Jellyfin, Calibre, Docker,
Music Assistant, Radarr, iRobot/rest980, Overseerr, Sonarr, Spotify), each with its own
`mcp-server` node (server description pre-filled, `Server URL`/`Identity provider` left
blank for you to fill in) and `mcp-in`/`mcp-out` tools — a good reference for wiring up
your own tools.

## Development

```
npm install
npm test
```

content.text:
Klart. Behörighetsmodellen är nu en enda regel, inga undantag någonstans.

**Vad som finns nu**

Ett claim-namn på servern, resten är kommaseparerade any-of-listor som AND:as ihop:

| Fält | Var | Begränsar |
|---|---|---|
| `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth | alla verktyg på servern |
| `Required value` | mcp-in *(ny)* | just det verktyget, utöver |
| `Required value` | mcp-server, Admin | `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`, utöver |

**Filer**

- [lib/claim-gate.js](lib/claim-gate.js) — ny. `grants` (primitiven, tom lista ger noll), `claimAllows` (tom lista = ingen restriktion), `createToolGate` (viker in serverlistan så den aldrig kan kringgås) och `visibleTools`. Ren och testbar — inget under `nodes/` var det tidigare.
- [lib/oauth-discovery.js:11](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L11) — `isAdmin` är nu bara ett alias för `claimAllows`. Den duplicerade gate-logiken är borta.
- [nodes/mcp-server.js](nodes/mcp-server.js) — `hasAccess` ersatt av en `gate` per request, `adminRequiredClaim` borttaget, per-tool-check i `initialize`, `tools/list` och `tools/call`.
- [nodes/mcp-in.js:26-30](nodes/mcp-in.js#L26-L30) + [.html](nodes/mcp-in.html) — nytt `requiredValue`-fält med hjälptext.
- [test/claim-gate.test.js](test/claim-gate.test.js) — 21 nya tester. Totalt 68 gröna.

**Verifierat på riktigt**, inte bara i enhetstest. Jag körde upp noden mot en fejkad Node-RED-runtime och drev den riktiga HTTP-handlern:

- serverlista tom → öppet verktyg + `admin`-gatat syns, `nope` är osynligt och nekas
- serverlista `admin, staff` → any-of matchar på serverfältet
- serverlista `staff` → allt nekas, verktygets egen lista hjälper inte. Det är AND:et som håller.
- adminlista `superuser` → admin-verktygen försvinner, vanliga verktyg opåverkade
- gammal `mcp-in` som anropar med fyra argument → verktyget förblir ogatat

**Två saker att känna till vid uppgradering**, båda dokumenterade i README: hade du satt ett *annat* claim-namn för admin-verktygen så matchar de nu mot Auth-flikens claim istället. Och ett värde som råkar innehålla ett kommatecken läses nu som en lista.

Kommandot `adminRequiredClaim: "groups"` låg i alla nio exempelflöden — identiskt med serverns, så borttagningen ändrade inget beteende där.

content.text:
Jag har hela kodbasen färsk i kontexten — alla noder, hela `lib/`, testerna och package.json. Här kommer båda delarna.

---

## Arkitektonisk review

**Det som är riktigt bra.** Grundformen är righteous: `nodes/` är tunt lim, `lib/` är ren, injicerbar logik utan Express/Node-RED-beroenden. Varje modul säger själv varför den finns och vilka trade-offs den gör — kommentarerna dokumenterar *beslut*, inte syntax. Säkerhetstänket är genomgående moget: constant-time-jämförelse som inte läcker längd ([mcp-auth.js:14](lib/mcp-auth.js#L14)), token-cache med hårt tak mot OOM-flooding ([mcp-auth.js:103](lib/mcp-auth.js#L103)), issuer/audience-pinning med motivering ([mcp-auth.js:130](lib/mcp-auth.js#L130)), redirect-URI-allowlist som aldrig ekar angriparens URI:er, rate-limits, `trust proxy`-varningen, id-charset-validering i admin-tools. Event-emitter-dispatchen via config-noden är idiomatisk Node-RED och gör `mcp-in`→flow→`mcp-out` naturligt asynkron. Designvalet att neka med `isError`-toolresultat istället för JSON-RPC-fel, så modellen får *läsa* varför, är genomtänkt och konsekvent.

**Strukturella observationer, viktigast först:**

### A1. Dispatchern bor i en 330-raders closure — den enda otestbara delen
`McpServer`-konstruktorn äger routes, auth-wiring, registry *och* hela JSON-RPC-switchen ([mcp-server.js:201-312](nodes/mcp-server.js#L201-L312)). Allt under `lib/` är exemplariskt testbart; precis logiken som avgör vad en caller får se och göra är det inte — jag fick bygga en fejkad RED-runtime för att röktesta gaten. Nästa naturliga extraktion enligt projektets egen stil: en `lib/mcp-rpc.js` med `handleRpc({ body, claims, gate, registry, adminTools }) → { status, result }`, och låt Express-handlern vara fem rader lim. Då kan Mocha nå `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`-besluten direkt.

### A2. `removeRoute` raderar grannens routes vid delad path
[mcp-server.js:40-46](nodes/mcp-server.js#L40-L46) filtrerar `_router.stack` på *path + metod*. Hela poängen med hostname-filtreringen är att flera `mcp-server`-noder delar samma path — men när nod A stängs (t.ex. en "modified nodes"-deploy som bara rör A) ryker även nod B:s route för `POST /mcp/<path>`, och B återregistrerar aldrig eftersom den inte deployats om. B är död tills nästa full deploy. Fixen är att göra borttagningen instansspecifik: tagga handlern (`handler._mcpOwner = node.id`) och filtrera på ägare, inte bara path. Att peta i `_router.stack` är redan en accepterad fulhack (Node-RED ger inget bättre), men den behöver vara kirurgisk.

### A3. Duplicerade toolName är en tyst konflikt
Två `mcp-in` med samma toolName på samma server: den andra skriver över registryposten, *båda* lyssnarna triggar på `mcp_tool_<name>` — två flöden kör, först till `mcp-out` vinner, den andra försvinner. Och när den ena noden tas bort avregistrerar dess `close` verktyget ([mcp-in.js:49](nodes/mcp-in.js#L49)) fast tvillingen lever — kvar finns en lyssnare utan registrypost, och verktyget blir "Unknown tool". Billig fix: låt `registerMCPTool` varna vid krock, och låt `unregisterMCPTool` bara radera om det är samma registrering (eller räkna referenser).

### A4. Protokollversionen står stilla
`protocolVersion: '2024-11-05'` är hårdkodad ([mcp-server.js:237](nodes/mcp-server.js#L237)) och `initialize` ekar den oavsett vad klienten begär. Spec:en har hunnit till 2025-06-18, och streamable-HTTP-klienter kan skicka `ping` (får `-32601` idag) och `GET` för SSE (får 404). Claude funkar idag, så ingen brådska — men det är den externa kontraktsytan, värd en rad i README och en bevakning. Minst: svara på `ping` med `{}`.

### A5. Förtroendegränsen för `msg.payload` är odokumenterad
`args` från callern går rakt in i flödet utan schemavalidering — JSON-schemat är bara dokumentation för modellen. Det är ett rimligt val (flödet är rätt ställe att validera), men hjälptexten varnar för claims-känslighet utan att säga det viktigare: **payload är angriparstyrd input**. Exemplen gör rätt (`encodeURIComponent`, Docker-API-anrop), men den som bygger `exec`-flöden behöver meningen i `mcp-in`-hjälpen och README.

---

## Code review

Rankat, allvarligast först. Jag har verifierat varje punkt mot koden, inte gissat.

### C1. `__proto__` som toolName smiter förbi "Unknown tool" — bug
[mcp-server.js:264](nodes/mcp-server.js#L264): `if (node.mcpRegisteredTools[toolName])` slår upp genom prototypkedjan. En autentiserad caller som skickar `params.name = "__proto__"` (eller `constructor`, `hasOwnProperty`…) får en truthy träff på `Object.prototype`, passerar gaten (`requiredValue` blir `undefined` → obegränsad), och hänger sedan i 30 sekunder på en emit ingen lyssnar på — istället för ett omedelbart `-32601`. Ingen krasch, men fel svar, en onödig pending-post per anrop och ett mönster som inte ska finnas i en internetexponerad dispatcher. Fix: `Object.create(null)` för registryt, eller `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(...)` vid uppslaget. (`visibleTools` går via `Object.entries` och är opåverkad; `mcpPendingCalls` nycklas med serversgenererad hex och är säker.)

### C2. `@atproto/api` skeppas till varje användare — fel sektion
[package.json:49](package.json#L49): `@atproto/api` ligger i `dependencies` men används bara av `scripts/bsky-announce.js` — som inte ens ingår i `files[]`. Varje `npm install` av noden drar in hela Bluesky-SDK:n i onödan. `postpublish` kör från repot, inte från det publicerade paketet, så flytta den till `devDependencies`.

### C3. `serverInfo.version` ljuger
[mcp-server.js:239](nodes/mcp-server.js#L239) rapporterar `'1.0.0'`; paketet är `0.3.1`. `require('../package.json').version` gör att klientloggar pekar på rätt release.

### C4. `initialize` duplicerar filtret som `visibleTools` redan äger
[mcp-server.js:230-235](nodes/mcp-server.js#L230-L235) gör entries→filter→map inline. `visibleTools(node.mcpRegisteredTools, gate).map(t => t.name)` ger samma namn från en enda källa — som dagens kod skulle en framtida ändring i synlighetsregeln behöva göras på två ställen. (Mitt verk från i förmiddags; borde ha återanvänt direkt.)

### C5. `isAdmin` är numera vestigial
Efter gate-refaktoreringen är [oauth-discovery.js:14](lib/oauth-discovery.js#L14) (`const isAdmin = claimAllows`) bara ett alias som enbart konsumeras av sin egen testsvit — produktion går via `claim-gate` direkt. Antingen radera exporten och flytta/ta bort testerna (täckningen finns redan i `claim-gate.test.js`), eller behåll medvetet som publik yta — men då förtjänar den en rad i README. Halvvägs-läget är det enda fel valet.

### C6. Skalära claims jämförs strikt mot strängar
[claim-gate.js:27](lib/claim-gate.js#L27): `v === w` — en IdP som skickar en numerisk claim (`{"level": 42}`) matchar aldrig konfigvärdet `"42"`. Grupper är i praktiken alltid strängar, så jag skulle lämna logiken orörd och bara nämna i hjälptexten att jämförelsen är strikt på strängar. Att börja typkonvertera i en auktoriseringsprimitiv vore fel riktning.

### C7. `maxBody` litar på Content-Length
[http-guards.js:46-53](lib/http-guards.js#L46-L53): chunked encoding har ingen Content-Length och passerar. Kommentaren kallar det redan "cheap early guard" och Node-REDs body-parser har egen limit bakom, så det håller — men en rad i modulkommentaren om att chunked går förbi vakten gör antagandet explicit.

### C8. Småplock
- [admin-tools.js:83](lib/admin-tools.js#L83): `tab.label` interpoleras rått i markdown till modellen — en flow-label kan injicera formatering/instruktioner. Flow-författaren är betrodd, så låg risk, men värt att veta.
- [mcp-out.js:31](nodes/mcp-out.js#L31): en array skickas obesiktigad som `content` — ett flöde som råkar returnera `[1,2,3]` ger ogiltiga MCP-content-block och ett kryptiskt klientfel. En rad i `mcp-out`-hjälpen ("arrayer måste vara MCP-content-block") räcker.
- Debug-tokenens claims är hårdkodade till `groups:['admin']` ([mcp-auth.js:120](lib/mcp-auth.js#L120)) — gater med andra värden än `admin` går inte att lokaltest utan riktig IdP. Ett konfigurerbart debug-claims-fält vore en liten DX-vinst.

---

## Sammanfattning

Solid, säkerhetsmedveten kodbas med ovanligt bra kommentarkultur — arkitekturen gör redan det mesta rätt. Det som faktiskt förtjänar handpåläggning: **C1** (`__proto__`-uppslaget, en riktig bug), **A2** (`removeRoute` sabbar host-filter-scenariot den ska möjliggöra), **C2** (onödig dependency till alla användare), och på sikt **A1** (lyft ut dispatchern så den blir testbar som resten). Resten är polish som kan tas när andan faller på.

Säg till om jag ska fixa några av punkterna — C1–C4 är tillsammans kanske tjugo minuters jobb.

# @frtnbach/node-red-contrib-mcp-server

Generic [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server nodes for
Node-RED: expose any flow as an MCP tool behind an OAuth-protected endpoint, with optional
Node-RED admin (flow read/deploy) tools. No home-automation or other domain coupling — this
is a bare building block for turning Node-RED flows into MCP tools that AI assistants
(Claude, etc.) can call.

## Nodes

- **`mcp-server`** (config node) — hosts a standalone MCP JSON-RPC endpoint at
  `POST /mcp/<path>`, OAuth 2.0 protected-resource discovery (RFC 9728), authorization-server
  discovery (RFC 8414) proxying a real OIDC identity provider, and a dynamic client
  registration shim, so OAuth-aware MCP clients (e.g. Claude.ai) can self-register and
  authenticate. Multiple `mcp-server` nodes can coexist, each with its own path and its own
  independent auth configuration.
- **`mcp-in`** — defines one MCP tool (name, description, JSON-Schema parameters, and an
  optional per-tool access gate). When an MCP client calls the tool, the node emits a message
  carrying the call arguments; wire the rest of the flow to do the actual work.
- **`mcp-out`** — resolves a pending tool call. Wire the end of your flow here with
  `msg._mcpCallId` intact (from the originating `mcp-in` message) and `msg.payload` set to
  the result.

A single `mcp-in` → ... → `mcp-out` chain is one MCP tool. Build as many chains as you want
against the same `mcp-server` node to expose a whole toolset.

## Admin tools

Enable **Admin tools** on an `mcp-server` node to additionally expose two tools that operate
on Node-RED's own Admin HTTP API, gated by a configurable JWT claim (default: `groups`
contains `admin`):

- **`get_flow`** — lists all flow tabs (id, label, node count), or returns the full JSON of
  one tab when called with an `id`.
- **`deploy_flow`** — creates or updates a flow tab.

## Configuring an `mcp-server` node

- **General**: name, `path` (→ registers `POST /mcp/<path>`), the public `Server URL` this
  Node-RED instance is reachable at, optional server name/instructions shown to the model, and
  an optional **hostname filter** (see below).
- **Auth**: an OIDC `Identity provider` issuer URL (**required** — endpoints auto-discovered
  from `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, with PocketID-style fallback paths; leaving this
  empty produces a broken OAuth discovery document with relative-path endpoints and no working
  auth, so the editor won't let you deploy without it), client id/secret (leave the secret
  empty to run as a public/PKCE client — recommended), **required** redirect URIs (defaults to
  Claude.ai's callback), scopes, token audience, an optional local debug token that bypasses
  the IdP entirely for local testing (put any placeholder URL in Identity provider and rely on
  the debug token — it's never contacted when the debug token matches), and the whole-server
  **required claim/value gate** (see below, unrelated despite the similar name).
- **Admin**: enable/disable admin tools, admin token (for the Node-RED Admin API), admin API
  port, and the required-value gate that additionally restricts just the admin tools.

### Access control

**One claim name, many value lists.** `Required claim` on the Auth tab (default `groups`) names
the single JWT claim every gate matches against. Every other authorization field is a
comma-separated **any-of** list of values — `media, ops` passes if the claim contains at least one
of them. An empty list imposes no restriction.

| Field | Where | Restricts |
|---|---|---|
| `Required value` | mcp-server, Auth tab | every tool on this server |
| `Required value` | mcp-in | that one tool, additionally |
| `Required value` | mcp-server, Admin tab | `get_flow`/`deploy_flow`, additionally |

**The lists are combined with AND.** Reaching a tool means clearing the server's list *and* that
tool's own list. Admin tools are not a special case — their field is simply the tool list for
`get_flow`/`deploy_flow`.

```
Required claim: groups     server value: staff
tool A: (empty)   tool B: media   admin value: admin

groups=[staff]         → A
groups=[staff, media]  → A, B
groups=[staff, admin]  → A + get_flow, deploy_flow
groups=[media]         → nothing            (server list not cleared)
groups=[guest]         → nothing

server value empty:
groups=[media]         → A, B
groups=[guest]         → A
```

Everyone with a valid token still connects — `initialize` always succeeds — but tools a caller
can't reach are hidden from `tools/list` and from the `initialize` instructions. A direct
`tools/call` on one of them is refused as an MCP tool result with `isError: true` and an
explanatory message (not a raw JSON-RPC protocol error), so the reason reaches the calling model
instead of being collapsed into a generic "tool execution failed".

> **Upgrading:** the admin gate no longer has its own claim-name field — it matches against the
> Auth tab's `Required claim` like everything else. If you had set a *different* claim name for
> admin tools, move that value to the Auth tab or adjust the admin list accordingly. A value that
> literally contains a comma is now read as a list rather than one literal string.

### Hostname filtering

Off by default. When **Only serve requests for this hostname** is enabled, the node only answers
requests whose `Host` header matches the hostname in its `Server URL`. This lets several
`mcp-server` nodes share the *same* `path` on one Node-RED instance, each answering only its own
virtual host — useful behind a reverse proxy that fronts multiple hostnames for one Node-RED
backend. Leave it off for a single server, or when a reverse proxy rewrites the `Host` header.

### Reverse proxy

Each `mcp-server` node is its own OAuth resource — unlike a single shared MCP endpoint, every
instance registers **its own** discovery and registration routes, scoped under its `path`. For
a node with `path: docker` and `Server URL: https://mcp.example.com`, these six routes exist:

| Method & path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /mcp/docker` | The JSON-RPC MCP endpoint (bearer-token protected) |
| `GET /mcp/docker/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` | Resource metadata (RFC 9728), path-inserted form |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/docker` | Resource metadata (RFC 9728), RFC 8414 form |
| `GET /mcp/docker/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | Auth-server metadata (RFC 8414), path-inserted form |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/docker` | Auth-server metadata (RFC 8414), RFC 8414 form |
| `POST /mcp/docker/oauth/register` | Dynamic client registration shim |

Both well-known forms are advertised because different MCP clients probe different ones —
expose both. Since every instance's routes share the `/mcp/<path>` and `/.well-known/*/mcp/<path>`
shapes, **one set of wildcard rules covers every current and future `mcp-server` node** (as long
as they're all reachable through the same domain/upstream) — no reverse-proxy change needed when
adding a new `path`. Example, using
[Caddy](https://caddyserver.com/) via [caddy-docker-proxy](https://github.com/lucaslorentz/caddy-docker-proxy)
labels:

```yaml
labels:
  caddy_1: mcp.example.com
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_0: /mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_1: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
  caddy_1.reverse_proxy_2: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/* "{{upstreams 1880}}"
```

Node-RED itself 404s any path that isn't an actual registered route, so the wildcard doesn't
expose anything beyond what each deployed `mcp-server` node already registers. If a `path`
needs to be reachable on a *different* domain than the others, give it its own `caddy_N` site
block (or combine with [hostname filtering](#hostname-filtering) above).

**What the identity provider needs to support** (same requirements as `lib/mcp-auth.js`):

- An **OIDC provider with discovery** — endpoints are read from
  `‹issuerUrl›/.well-known/openid-configuration`, falling back to PocketID's path layout if
  discovery is unavailable.
- **JWT access tokens** signed with a key published on the provider's **JWKS** (tokens are
  verified locally; opaque/introspection-only access tokens are not supported).
- A client configured with the **redirect URI(s)** from the node's *Redirect URIs* setting,
  grant types `authorization_code` + `refresh_token`, **PKCE (S256)**, and — if a client secret
  is set — `client_secret_post` auth. Leave the secret empty to run as a public/PKCE client
  (recommended).

> Tested with **Caddy** (reverse proxy) + **PocketID** (identity provider) + **Claude.ai** (MCP
> client). Any spec-compliant OIDC provider issuing JWT access tokens, behind any reverse proxy
> that forwards the routes above, should work the same way.

## Examples

See [`examples/`](examples/) for nine ready-to-import flows (Jellyfin, Calibre, Docker,
Music Assistant, Radarr, iRobot/rest980, Overseerr, Sonarr, Spotify), each with its own
`mcp-server` node (server description pre-filled, `Server URL`/`Identity provider` left
blank for you to fill in) and `mcp-in`/`mcp-out` tools — a good reference for wiring up
your own tools.

## Development

```
npm install
npm test
```

## License
